_comment: Hand-authored corrections applied AFTER generation by tools/refresh-thresholds.ts. 'patch' merges into a generated row by code; 'add' appends rows Stripe has no concept of; 'drop' removes generated rows. Patching clears needs_review unless the patch sets one, so every entry here is a recorded human decision.

US-CA.note: SaaS generally not taxable in CA; electronically delivered software/products vary. Taxability needs human review.

US-TX.note: SaaS taxable as data processing (80% of charge) in TX.

US-WA.note: Digital products and SaaS broadly taxable in WA.

US-FL.note: Measured on the PREVIOUS calendar year — the default trailing-12m fetch window cannot fully cover it; treat this row as indicative. Electronically delivered software generally not taxable in FL.

US-CO.note: SaaS is NOT taxable at the Colorado state level. Colorado's ~70 home-rule cities (Denver, Boulder and others) administer their own sales tax and several DO tax SaaS — those local registrations are a separate obligation and are not modeled here.

US-GA.note: Either leg triggers (revenue OR 200 transactions). SaaS and electronically delivered software are generally NOT taxable in GA; taxability needs human review.

US-NJ.note: Either leg triggers (revenue OR 200 transactions). NJ taxes prewritten software delivered electronically, but exempts SaaS used exclusively for business purposes — taxability needs human review.

JP.note: Threshold measured against the 'base period' (two fiscal years prior) — approximated as trailing 12 months here; flagged for human review.

SG.note: Dual test: SGD 100,000 of B2C supplies into Singapore AND global turnover above SGD 1,000,000. Stripe's published figure leads with the global leg; the Singapore leg is the one scored here, because the global leg cannot be measured from Stripe charges alone.

GB.note: Non-established businesses (NETPs) have NO registration threshold — liability from the first taxable UK sale. The GBP 90,000 threshold applies only to UK-established businesses.

US-NY.note: Both legs must be met in NY: revenue OVER USD 500,000 AND MORE THAN 100 sales — so 100 sales exactly does not trigger. Measured over the four IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING New York sales tax quarters (Dec-Feb, Mar-May, Jun-Aug, Sep-Nov), which are not calendar quarters and exclude the current, incomplete quarter. SaaS is generally taxable in NY.

US-PA.note: Measured over the PREVIOUS 12-MONTH PERIOD (Sales Tax Bulletin 2019-01), not a calendar year. Digital products and SaaS taxable in PA.

CH.note: Stripe publishes CHF 100,000 per rolling 12 months. The statutory test is GLOBAL turnover, not Swiss turnover — a business with CHF 100k worldwide revenue and any Swiss sales is liable. Modelled here against Swiss revenue only, which is conservative in the other direction.

review_reasons: Stripe prints '2,00,000 ZAR' — Indian lakh digit grouping on a rand figure, so the value is not trustworthy as written.
SARS' published threshold for foreign electronic services suppliers is understood to be ZAR 1,000,000. Confirm against the tax authority before shipping this row.
Stripe states 'past or next 12 months'. The forward-looking leg cannot be modelled from historical charges — this row tests the backward leg only and will under-report.

US-DE.note: Delaware levies no state sales tax. No registration obligation arises from sales volume.

US-MT.note: Montana levies no state sales tax. No registration obligation arises from sales volume.

US-NH.note: New Hampshire levies no state sales tax. No registration obligation arises from sales volume.

US-OR.note: Oregon levies no state sales tax. No registration obligation arises from sales volume.

HK.note: Hong Kong levies no VAT, GST or sales tax. No registration obligation arises from sales volume.

AU.note: AUD 75,000 in the previous or current year. Stripe also notes an AUD 150,000 variant for non-profit organisations, which is not modelled — a non-profit merchant will be over-flagged.

US-AK.note: Alaska has no statewide sales tax; the 100,000 USD figure is the ARSSTC statewide standard adopted by local jurisdictions, which may vary it. Treat this row as indicative of local, not state, obligations.

LK.note: Stripe writes the currency as 'RS'; read as LKR.

add.note: Scheme-aware at compute time: non-EU established merchants get the non-Union OSS scheme (no threshold, liability from first B2C sale); EU-established merchants get Union OSS (EUR 10,000 micro-threshold on cross-border B2C, domestic sales excluded). Domestic VAT obligations are out of scope.
Provincial regimes (QC, BC, SK, MB) have separate rules not in this starter dataset.
